question: Will Safe Superintelligence (SSI) release an AI model to the public in 2026?

calls.reasoning: Status quo is No: SSI has shipped nothing in 2+ years and its stated strategy is a 'straight-shot' with one product. The August 2026 release rumours (Gavin Baker podcast, Casado hints) did not happen and were never confirmed by SSI. Under two months remain with no waitlist, API or announcement visible as of late Oct 2026. Upside: Sutskever said SSI might deploy before superintelligence, and NVIDIA's ~$5B and new compute suggest the work is maturing. But 'scale up' points to more training first, and a 'gradual release' may begin as a closed beta, which does not count. Polymarket's Dec-31 market (~20c, about $142k across the related markets) looks like the same contract but sits oddly against its Nov-30 sibling at 1c, and that crowd has been overoptimistic before (the Oct-31 market was at 53% and resolved No), so I stay below it.
calls.dossier:
- Status (aitoolsreview.co.uk and other summaries, Oct 2026): as of 26 Oct 2026 SSI had released no model, API, paper, waitlist or product. Founded June 2024.
- SSI mission text (ssi.inc): 'one goal and one product: a safe superintelligence'; 'straight-shot' lab.
- Nov 2025 Dwarkesh podcast: Sutskever said superintelligence is 5-20 yrs away, SSI might deploy a model before then, and any release would be 'gradual'.
- 27 Jul 2026 (NVIDIA newsroom/TechCrunch): NVIDIA partnership, ~$5B investment, Vera Rubin access to raise SSI compute 'by an order of magnitude'. Sutskever: 'we have research that is worthy of scaling up'.
- Early Aug 2026: investor Gavin Baker (Invest Like the Best podcast) said SSI would release its model in August. Single second-hand source, never confirmed by SSI.
- 25-26 Aug 2026 (BigGo Finance): Martin Casado (a16z) teased 'the most important model release of the year'; observers hinted at a continual-learning breakthrough from a 'non-frontier lab'. Nothing from SSI followed.
- Reported technical bet: test-time training / continual learning (secondary sources, unverified).
- Polymarket event 'SSI public model released by ...' (opened 22 Sep 2026): the Oct-31 leg had traded around a coin-flip and resolved No. Current leg prices are in the forecaster's reasoning, not here. Manifold has only an unrelated benchmark market.
- Resolution instrument: resolves off credible reports that the general public can use an official SSI model (free or paid). Announcements, closed betas and demos do not count; geo or ID restrictions are fine.
- Event window: question opened 2026-10-26 -> deadline 2027-01-01 00:00 PT. As of 2026-11-03, about 12% of that window has elapsed (~58 days remain). Relative to SSI's whole history (Jun 2024 onward), there have been 0 public releases in ~29 months.
- For Yes: big new compute and funding, Sutskever is open to an interim release, and repeated insider rumours of an imminent model.
- For No: the stated straight-shot strategy, every dated rumour so far has failed, 'scale up' implies more training first, and a gradual or closed-beta start would not count.
- Searched, could not find: any official SSI announcement, waitlist, API docs, product job postings, or a reported December launch date; no news dated November 2026.
calls.reference_class: Stealth frontier-lab startups with no product after 2 years, plus repeated unconfirmed release rumours; chance of a first public release in a given 2-month window

calls.reasoning: Status quo: SSI has shipped no model, API, paper or product in about 28 months, and it describes itself as a 'straight-shot' lab with one product. The August 2026 release rumour from Gavin Baker never materialized, and as of late October SSI's own channels show nothing. Only about 2 months remain (Nov 3 to Jan 1). Arguments for Yes: NVIDIA's July 2026 partnership adds a lot of compute, Sutskever has said a public model before superintelligence is possible, and an investor claimed a release was coming. Human markets: the Polymarket contract 'SSI public model released by December 31, 2026' trades around 20-21% on a thin book. The companion 'by November 30' contract trades at about 1%, which implies a December-only hazard of roughly 19%. That looks inconsistent, so I discount the December market as thin and optimistic. Sutskever's stated preference for a 'gradual release' also suggests a first release might be a closed or limited beta, which would not count under this question.
